# Intent - phase-b

Written 2026-11-02 by randlee and Codex.

## What this plan is for

Phase B turns the existing atm-shpherd product definition and client prototype into a working sc-runtime application. It begins with an untouched, tested sc-runtime 0.1.1 `sqlite-postgres` generation, then ports the current scmux schema, business behavior, and web UI into the Shpherd architecture.

The execution-ready boundary map, wave table, and sprint documents are indexed by `phase-b-plan.md`. The locked anchor record remains `anchors.json`; hardening may reorganize sprint ownership but may not weaken or replace those anchors.

Shpherd manages teams across computers through a local SQLite database synchronized with shared PostgreSQL state. Herdr is the default launcher; tmux remains an explicitly supported backend. The plan preserves scmux behavior first, then adds the minimum app-owned fields and adapters needed for Herdr, ATM roster management, multi-host operation, and later scheduling.

## What success looks like

- The generated sc-runtime baseline passes setup, lint, test, CLI-build, and daemon-build gates before scmux migration begins.
- The `shpherd` CLI and `atm-shpherd` daemon reproduce the retained scmux schema, definition management, observation, launcher, and browser/Tauri UI behavior.
- A team launches through Herdr by default and through tmux when explicitly configured.
- SQLite-to-PostgreSQL synchronization makes team definitions available for safe launch on another authorized host.
- The repository upgrades to sc-runtime 0.2.0 immediately after release, including its dependency refresh and complete sc-lint 0.8.4-or-newer consumer installation.

## What is deliberately out of scope

- AI chat, ontology generation, OxyGraph context providers, and schema-derived agent context graphs.
- Replacing app-owned Shpherd schema, synchronization, launcher, or ATM policy with sc-runtime responsibilities.
- Exact visual redesign beyond porting the retained scmux UI behavior into the existing browser/Tauri client.

## Anchors

Anchors for this plan live in `anchors.json` (record of truth) and are rendered to `anchors.md`. Requirements and ADRs that govern this plan are listed there too, under their own IDs.

records.statement: Phase B PostgreSQL must provide a fleet-wide view of teams across all computers.
records.quote: The postgresdb is simply a view of all teams on all computers.
records.scope: Phase B beads that define PostgreSQL schema, host synchronization, fleet views, or launch coordination.
records.check: PostgreSQL schema and boundary tests expose a fleet-wide team view and no launch-lease or launch-authority operation.

pass: PostgreSQL displays teams from rand-m4 and rand-m5 together in one fleet view.
fail: PostgreSQL grants a global team launch lease and rejects a second computer running the same named team.

records.summary: Keep PostgreSQL as fleet read model
records.deterministic_check: PostgreSQL schema and boundary tests expose a fleet-wide team view and no launch-lease or launch-authority operation.
records.context: Phase B architecture clarification in Codex

cases.text: PostgreSQL displays teams from rand-m4 and rand-m5 together in one fleet view.
cases.rationale: Approved pass fixture: combines teams on two computers in fleet view.

cases.text: PostgreSQL grants a global team launch lease and rejects a second computer running the same named team.
cases.rationale: Approved fail fixture and check forbid PostgreSQL launch authority; it contains no fleet-view commitment.

cases.text: PostgreSQL exposes a fleet-wide view of teams across all computers.

cases.rationale: PostgreSQL schema lies in scope but no view or authority policy is specified.

cases.text: Document the PostgreSQL fleet-view endpoint name, without specifying which teams or computers its result includes.
cases.rationale: A topical endpoint name does not commit to fleet coverage; omission is not conflict.

cases.text: The PostgreSQL team view intentionally contains only this computer's teams and excludes teams on every other computer.
cases.rationale: Explicit single-computer restriction conflicts with all-computers view.

cases.text: Adjust the logo spacing in the browser header CSS.
cases.rationale: Presentation spacing neither affects nor depends on PostgreSQL fleet behavior.

cases.text: Show teams from rand-m4 and rand-m5 together in the PostgreSQL fleet view. Retain both entries when team names match and permit both computers to run their respective teams; PostgreSQL grants no launch authority.
cases.rationale: Two-computer view satisfies statement and same-name independent launch follows approved fail boundary.

cases.text: When PostgreSQL is unavailable the CLI displays its local cached teams. When connected, the PostgreSQL fleet view displays teams across all computers.
cases.rationale: Local offline display does not narrow the PostgreSQL fleet view; no new availability requirement is invented.

cases.text: PostgreSQL displays all teams from all computers together in a fleet view, and grants a global team launch lease that rejects a second computer running the same named team.
cases.rationale: Presence and conflict are independent: fleet view is stated but approved launch-authority boundary is broken.
